referenceManifest.build: pnpm install && pnpm --filter "vue-lynx..." build && cd packages/benchmark && node harness/build-unified.mjs --only=vdom-ifr-et,vapor-ifr,react

vdom-ifr-et.description: Vue Lynx vdom top config (vdom +b +ifr; legacy id vdom-ifr-et)

vapor-ifr.description: Vue Lynx vapor top config (vapor +b +ifr; legacy id vapor-ifr)

referenceManifest.note: Black-box fixtures: only the .web.bundle files are vendored. They are served unmodified into <lynx-view> by web/run-web.mjs; the app workloads mirror app/src operation-for-operation. The harness host runs @lynx-js/web-core 0.22.2 for every cell (the fork built against 0.22.1 — the host runtime is shared, so the comparison stays same-host).

firstScreen.description: ReactLynx built with a pre-populated first screen, one bundle per row count. The `react` cell above measures startup and create@N from a click; this set is what makes FCP@N measurable for a reference at all, because a pre-populated first screen is a build-time define of the app source and cannot be produced from the shipping bundle.
firstScreen.note: A DIFFERENT ARTIFACT FROM THE `react` CELL, and deliberately so: a different vue-lynx commit and a different @lynx-js/react (0.124.0 against the `react` cell's 0.122.1). It is vendored beside that cell rather than replacing it, so every number the featured runs recorded against `react` keeps its bundle. Both are measured in the same window when a run asks for both, and the create-window host calls per row are the control that says whether the two workloads still agree operation-for-operation. Hashes are the ones the campaign entry pinned; they were re-verified on copy.

meta.protocol: fresh page per sample; control/counts/timed order rotates across repetitions in one host window; startup and create are measured in the same page load; the probe is host-side, so every variant runs the same framework bundle
